subject: ela
intro: Read both passages in each item, then choose the best answer. Each item gives you everything you need, so you do not have to read anything outside the page.

items.prompt:
Read both passages, then answer the question.

Passage 1 (from Maya Chen's memoir): "I still remember the first time I flew my drone over the canyon. My hands shook on the controller. When the camera sent back a picture of the river far below, I forgot to breathe. I had built that drone in my garage for two years, and now it was really flying."

Passage 2 (from a magazine profile of Maya Chen): "Maya Chen spent two years building a camera drone in her home garage. In 2019, she flew it over a local canyon to photograph the river. The flight made her one of the youngest people in her state to win a science prize for engineering."

What event do both passages describe?
A) Maya Chen winning a science prize at an awards ceremony
B) Maya Chen flying her homemade drone over the canyon
C) Maya Chen learning to repair drones for other people
D) Maya Chen building a drone over the course of two years and then giving up
items.answer: B) Maya Chen flying her homemade drone over the canyon

steps: Both passages center on the same moment: Maya flying the drone she built over the canyon. The memoir describes how it felt, and the profile reports it as a fact, so B is the shared event.
A is wrong because only Passage 2 mentions the science prize, and even there the prize is a result, not the event both texts describe.
C is wrong because neither passage says she repaired drones for other people; this detail appears in neither text.
D is wrong because she did not give up; both passages say the drone flew, so this misreads the texts.
solution.answer: B) Maya Chen flying her homemade drone over the canyon

items.prompt:
Read both passages, then answer the question.

Passage 1 (a firsthand account by sailor Tom Reed): "The storm hit us at dawn. Waves taller than our mast crashed over the deck. I tied myself to the wheel so I would not be swept away. For six hours I steered while the rain stung my face."

Passage 2 (from a newspaper report): "On Tuesday, the fishing boat Sea Star was caught in a sudden storm at dawn. The captain steered the boat to safety after about six hours. All four crew members survived."

Which author wrote a firsthand account, and which wrote an outside report?
A) Both Tom Reed and the newspaper wrote firsthand accounts
B) The newspaper wrote firsthand and Tom Reed wrote the outside report
C) Tom Reed wrote the firsthand account and the newspaper wrote the outside report
D) Neither passage is firsthand; both are outside reports
items.answer: C) Tom Reed wrote the firsthand account and the newspaper wrote the outside report

steps: Tom Reed uses "I" and "us" and describes what he felt and did during the storm, so he was a participant writing a firsthand account. The newspaper reports the event from the outside, naming the boat and the crew, so C is correct.
A is wrong because the newspaper is an outside report, not firsthand; it never uses "I" about being on the boat.
B is wrong because it swaps the two authors, treating the outside report as firsthand and the participant as the observer.
D is wrong because Passage 1 is clearly firsthand, shown by Reed's use of "I" and his description of his own actions.
solution.answer: C) Tom Reed wrote the firsthand account and the newspaper wrote the outside report

items.prompt:
Read both passages, then answer the question.

Passage 1 (from a beekeeper's journal): "This morning I opened the hive and counted three new frames of honey. The bees were calm. I wore my veil but no gloves, which I prefer because I can feel the comb. I harvested two jars."

Passage 2 (from a 4-H club newsletter): "Club member Dana Ortiz checked her hive this morning and harvested two jars of honey. Dana has kept bees for three years and teaches a beginner class each spring."

Which fact do BOTH passages state?
A) Dana wore a veil but no gloves
B) Dana harvested two jars of honey
C) Dana has kept bees for three years
D) Dana teaches a beginner class each spring
items.answer: B) Dana harvested two jars of honey

steps: The journal says "I harvested two jars" and the newsletter says Dana "harvested two jars of honey," so both texts report this same fact, making B correct.
A is wrong because only the journal mentions the veil and gloves; the newsletter does not.
C is wrong because only the newsletter says she has kept bees for three years.
D is wrong because only the newsletter mentions the beginner class; choosing a detail from just one text is a common error.
solution.answer: B) Dana harvested two jars of honey

items.prompt:
Read both passages, then answer the question.

Passage 1 (from astronaut Lena Park's memoir): "When the rocket's engines lit, my whole body pressed back into the seat. My heart pounded so hard I could hear it over the roar. I thought of my mother waving from the crowd. Then the shaking smoothed out, and suddenly Earth was a curved blue line below me. I had trained nine years for this, and no training had prepared me for how small and bright our planet looked."

Passage 2 (from a science encyclopedia): "Lena Park launched aboard a rocket in 2021 after nine years of training. The launch reached orbit in about nine minutes. From orbit, astronauts observe Earth's curvature and atmosphere. Park's mission lasted six months and gathered data on plant growth in low gravity."

What does the memoir include about the launch that the encyclopedia leaves out?
A) That Park trained for nine years before the launch
B) How the launch felt to Park, including her pounding heart and her thoughts of her mother
C) That the mission gathered data on plant growth
D) That the launch reached orbit in about nine minutes
items.answer: B) How the launch felt to Park, including her pounding heart and her thoughts of her mother

steps: The memoir describes Park's inner experience: her body pressed back, her pounding heart, her thoughts of her mother, and her awe at Earth. The encyclopedia reports only facts and dates and leaves these feelings out, so B is the difference.
A is wrong because both texts mention the nine years of training, so it is shared, not unique to the memoir.
C is wrong because the plant-growth data appears only in the encyclopedia, the opposite of what the question asks.
D is wrong because the nine-minute detail is in the encyclopedia, not the memoir.
solution.answer: B) How the launch felt to Park, including her pounding heart and her thoughts of her mother

items.prompt:
Read both passages, then answer the question.

Passage 1 (from firefighter Rosa Vega's first-person account): "We reached the apartment building at 2 a.m. Smoke was already pouring from the third floor. I climbed the ladder while my partner held it steady. Inside, I crawled low under the heat and found a frightened child near a window. I carried her down to her parents, who were crying with relief."

Passage 2 (from a city news bulletin): "A fire broke out early Thursday in a third-floor apartment. Firefighters responded within minutes and rescued one child. No injuries were reported. Officials are investigating the cause, which may have been an overloaded power strip."

Why can Rosa Vega's account describe how the rescue felt and looked up close, while the news bulletin focuses on facts like the time and the cause?
A) Because Vega was a firsthand participant in the rescue, while the bulletin reports from the outside
B) Because the bulletin was written before the fire happened
C) Because Vega had less information about the fire than the news reporter did
D) Because the bulletin author was also inside the burning building
items.answer: A) Because Vega was a firsthand participant in the rescue, while the bulletin reports from the outside

steps: Vega was inside the rescue, so she can describe the smoke, the ladder, the frightened child, and the crying parents from direct experience. The bulletin reports from the outside, so it gives facts like the time and the suspected cause. Their different relationships to the event explain the difference, so A is correct.
B is wrong because the bulletin reports the fire as a past event, not before it happened.
C is wrong because Vega's closeness gave her more, not less, of the sensory detail; the difference is point of view, not amount of information.
D is wrong because nothing suggests the bulletin author was inside; it is an outside report.
solution.answer: A) Because Vega was a firsthand participant in the rescue, while the bulletin reports from the outside

items.prompt:
Read both passages, then answer the question.

Passage 1 (from inventor Amir Haddad's memoir): "People think the hard part of inventing the water filter was the science. For me it was the failures. I built forty versions that clogged or leaked. My family thought I should quit. The night the forty-first version finally ran clear, I sat on the floor and laughed until I cried."

Passage 2 (from a textbook): "Amir Haddad developed a low-cost water filter that is now used in many villages. The device removes bacteria using layers of sand and charcoal. It can clean up to twenty liters of water per day and costs little to build."

How do the authors' purposes differ?
A) Both authors mainly want to explain how the filter removes bacteria
B) Both authors mainly want to share the emotional story of inventing the filter
C) Haddad's purpose is to share his personal struggle and feelings, while the textbook's purpose is to explain the filter's design and uses
D) The textbook's purpose is to share Haddad's personal struggle, while Haddad's purpose is to explain how the filter works
items.answer: C) Haddad's purpose is to share his personal struggle and feelings, while the textbook's purpose is to explain the filter's design and uses

steps: Haddad writes about his many failures, his family's doubt, and his relief, so his purpose is personal and emotional. The textbook explains how the filter works and what it does, so its purpose is to inform about the device. That contrast makes C correct.
A is wrong because only the textbook explains the bacteria-removal process; the memoir does not focus on the science.
B is wrong because only the memoir tells the emotional story; the textbook does not.
D is wrong because it swaps the two purposes, giving the textbook's job to the memoir and the memoir's job to the textbook.
solution.answer: C) Haddad's purpose is to share his personal struggle and feelings, while the textbook's purpose is to explain the filter's design and uses

items.prompt:
Read both passages, then answer the question.

Passage 1 (from coach Bea Lansing's memoir): "That championship game still feels like a dream I cannot quite trust. We were down by ten points with four minutes left, and I could see my players' shoulders dropping. So I called a timeout and did not talk about plays at all. I told them I was proud of them no matter what the scoreboard said. Something shifted. They went back out loose and laughing, and they scored twelve straight points. People say I am a brilliant strategist, but the truth is the win came from a moment of letting go, not a clever play. I have coached for thirty years, and that timeout taught me more than any drill ever did."

Passage 2 (from a sports website article): "Coach Bea Lansing led the Hawks to the state title in a stunning comeback. Trailing by ten with four minutes remaining, Lansing called a timeout and reset her team, which then scored twelve unanswered points to win. Analysts praised Lansing's sharp tactical adjustments down the stretch. Over her thirty-year career, she has won four state titles and is known for her detailed game plans."

How does the difference in the authors' points of view lead to a different overall impression of why the comeback happened?
A) The memoir credits the comeback to an emotional, encouraging moment, while the article credits it to Lansing's tactical adjustments, so each leaves a different impression of the cause
B) Both texts agree the comeback was caused by a clever play Lansing drew up during the timeout
C) The memoir credits sharp tactics while the article credits an emotional moment, reversing the two views
D) Neither text offers any explanation for why the comeback happened
items.answer: A) The memoir credits the comeback to an emotional, encouraging moment, while the article credits it to Lansing's tactical adjustments, so each leaves a different impression of the cause

steps: Lansing, writing from the inside, says the win came from a moment of letting go and encouraging her players, not a clever play. The outside article credits her "sharp tactical adjustments." Because each author sees the event differently, readers get two different impressions of the cause, so A is correct.
B is wrong because Lansing explicitly denies a clever play caused the win, so the texts do not agree on that.
C is wrong because it reverses the two views; the memoir is the emotional one and the article is the tactical one, not the other way around.
D is wrong because both texts do explain the comeback, just in different ways, so saying neither explains it ignores the texts.
solution.answer: A) The memoir credits the comeback to an emotional, encouraging moment, while the article credits it to Lansing's tactical adjustments, so each leaves a different impression of the cause

items.prompt:
Read both passages, then answer the question.

Passage 1 (from naturalist Otis Bell's field memoir): "For three winters I tracked the lone wolf the locals called Gray. I came to know her trails, her resting spots, the way she paused at the ridge each evening. When she finally disappeared one March, I felt I had lost a friend. I cannot prove she died; she may simply have moved on to new territory. But I missed her, and that grief taught me how attached a person can become to a wild animal he has only watched from a distance."

Passage 2 (from a wildlife agency report): "Wolf G-7, a female, was monitored in the northern range for three seasons. Tracking data show consistent movement patterns until March, when the signal was lost. The collar may have failed, or the animal may have left the monitored area. No carcass was recovered. The case is listed as unresolved."

What does reading BOTH passages together give a reader that reading only one would not?
A) Only the report tells the reader the wolf was female, so the memoir adds nothing
B) The two texts disagree about whether the wolf died, so a reader cannot learn anything reliable from either
C) Together, the memoir's firsthand attachment and grief and the report's tracking data give both the human meaning and the factual record of the same disappearance, a fuller picture than either alone
D) Both texts say the wolf certainly died, so reading both only repeats the same conclusion twice
items.answer: C) Together, the memoir's firsthand attachment and grief and the report's tracking data give both the human meaning and the factual record of the same disappearance, a fuller picture than either alone

steps: The memoir gives the human side, Bell's attachment and grief, while the report gives the factual record, the tracking data and the unresolved status. Read together they cover both the meaning and the facts of the same disappearance, so C is correct.
A is wrong because the memoir adds the firsthand emotional understanding the report lacks, so it does add value.
B is wrong because the texts do not truly disagree; both say the cause is unknown, so a reader can still learn a great deal.
D is wrong because neither text says the wolf certainly died; both leave the outcome open, so the claim misreads them.
solution.answer: C) Together, the memoir's firsthand attachment and grief and the report's tracking data give both the human meaning and the factual record of the same disappearance, a fuller picture than either alone
